name: University of Birmingham
feeMethod: Sets a separate fee for each course, so the calculator uses each course's own published fee.
description: The University of Birmingham received its royal charter in 1900, growing out of Mason Science College, and was England's first civic 'red brick' university. It is a member of the Russell Group, with its main campus at Edgbaston.
whyIncluded: Birmingham has taught degrees in Singapore for over two decades and partnered SIM from 2009, welcoming more than 1,900 Singapore-based students by 2014. Its law degree is recognised by the Singapore Institute of Legal Education for practice in Singapore.

livingCosts.summary: The university's own weekly budget for a 42-week year: a self-catered university room with bills included, food and toiletries, travel, course costs and social spending. Deposits, insurance and the TV licence are left out.
livingCosts.notes: Rung A. University of Birmingham Money Advice 'Living costs' page, 'Essential weekly costs (based on a 42-week academic session)' and 'Variable weekly costs (average)'. Weekly figures converted to monthly at 52/12 (x4.3333); months = 10 because 42 weeks is 9.7 months. Housing = 'Self Catered (Univ.)' rent GBP 150/week with gas, electric, water and Wi-Fi included (meal-plan halls are 175 incl. food; a private house is 100 rent + 11 gas/electric + 3 water). Food = food 50 + toiletries 5 + laundry 5 = 60/week. Transport = 'Travel' 25/week. Personal = course costs 18 + social/memberships 50 + clothing 10 + mobile 2 = 80/week (internet 5 excluded because the page says it is not needed in university accommodation). Excluded: one-off initial costs (deposit up to 550, bedding, possessions insurance 80, TV licence 154.50, police registration 34). The page states no academic year; some one-off items (police registration, TV licence 154.50) are pre-2022 rates, so the page may not have been refreshed recently; year set to the current 2026/27 page.

programmes.feeBasis: Birmingham's own 2026/27 fact-sheet international fee of £30,600 a year for this MEng; the 2027 fee is still 'to be confirmed'.

programmes.summary: Yearly tuition for international students starting in 2026, from Birmingham's 2026/27 programme fact sheet (the 2027 international fee is not yet published). Birmingham keeps the first-year fee for the whole course.
programmes.notes: Secondary source: Birmingham's course pages show only the UK fee as text and put the international fee behind a country selector that is not readable without JavaScript; the international fees pages (study/international/fees, study/undergraduate/fees-funding/tuition, study/postgraduate/taught/fees-funding/taught-fees) give no figures, the UCAS entry lists the UK fee only, and no official fee table or PDF could be found (checked 2026-10-07). Figure read from the Studyportals listing for University of Birmingham (Birmingham, UK campus, not Dubai), start date 27 September 2027, '30,600 GBP / year'. Replace with the official figure when it can be read. Studyportals lists the programme as 'Mechanical Engineering (Hons)', MEng, 48 months. Fee policy (official, birmingham.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/fees-funding/tuition, read 2026-10-07): 'The fee paid in your first year will remain constant with no inflationary increase for the duration of your course, with the exception of the International Foundation Programme and clinical courses', so cohortLocked is true. No compulsory fees besides tuition. No feeHistory rows: on 2026-10-13 the course page still showed only the UK fee (international fee behind the country selector) and searches found no official or year-dated figure for 2024, 2025 or 2026 entry (aggregators such as Hotcourses show only the 2027 fee). 2024-2026 rows still unfilled (2026-10-13, unofficial search): Unienrol, Tutopiya, Collegedunia and Studyportals give only undated or 2027/next-intake fees, Kaplan lists foundation-year fees only, and the official course page still shows UK fees for 2027 entry only. Round 3 (2026-10-13): the legacy .aspx course pages show only UK fees for 2027 starts (international fees sit behind a country selector); no year-dated Birmingham fee PDF or FOI reply was found. Round 4 (2026-10-13): the legacy postgraduate .aspx course pages and undergraduate/fees/fees.aspx give no international figures; still unfilled. Round 5 (2026-10-13): Birmingham's official Programme Fact Sheets (CMA course information PDFs, listed at birmingham.ac.uk/undergraduate/programme-factsheets/<year>-course-information) give the annual tuition fee for each entry year: 2024/25 sheet 'International: £28,560'; 2025/26 sheet 'International: £29,560'; 2026/27 sheet 'International: £30,600'. Added these as official rows. The 2026/27 fact-sheet figure equals the Studyportals figure in `fees`, and the official course page (CMS record 'UG 2027 ...') shows the 2027/28 international fee as 'To be confirmed', so `fees` probably holds the 2026 entry fee (corrected later in this note). Round 5 (2026-10-13): Birmingham's course page lists the 2027 international fee as 'To be confirmed', and the Bachelorsportal '2027' figure (£30,600) is exactly the official 2026/27 fact-sheet fee. The programme is therefore now priced at feeYear 2026 from the official fact sheet, and the duplicate 2026 feeHistory row was removed; a 2027 start is projected by the calculator until Birmingham publishes it.

programmes.summary: Tuition for international students on the one-year full-time master's starting in September 2027, from Birmingham's own course page. No separate compulsory fees.
programmes.notes: Secondary source: Birmingham's course pages show only the UK fee as text and put the international fee behind a country selector that is not readable without JavaScript; the international fees pages (study/international/fees, study/undergraduate/fees-funding/tuition, study/postgraduate/taught/fees-funding/taught-fees) give no figures, the UCAS entry lists the UK fee only, and no official fee table or PDF could be found (checked 2026-10-07). Replace with the official figure when it can be read. 12 months full-time. Conversion MSc for graduates from other subjects. No compulsory fees besides tuition. Round 3 (2026-10-13): the legacy .aspx course pages show only UK fees for 2027 starts (international fees sit behind a country selector); no year-dated Birmingham fee PDF or FOI reply was found. Round 4 (2026-10-13): the legacy postgraduate .aspx course pages and undergraduate/fees/fees.aspx give no international figures; still unfilled. Round 5 (2026-10-13): the course page HTML still embeds the previous course record, whose fees text reads 'Annual Tuition fees for 2024/25 ... International students: £31,410'. Added 2024 row (official). The official 2027 fee is '£34,740 January 2027 / £36,000 September 2027'; `fees` holds the January figure (corrected later in this note). 2025 and 2026 not found. Round 5 (2026-10-13): current fee corrected to the official figure. The Birmingham course page gives the international fee as £36,000 (full-time) for 2027 entry ('Fees for 2027 entry are above'); the Mastersportal figure previously used (£34,740) was lower. A January 2027 start costs less; the September figure is used. Round 6 (2026-10-13): rechecked Birmingham's CMS: fee records exist only for 2026/27 bands and January 2026 starts, the legacy '.inc' fee snippets are not served (404), and the university fee-summary PDFs (2024-25, 2025-26) cover home fees only; WebSearch found only undated aggregator figures. Remaining years still unfilled. Round 7 (2026-10-13, Common Crawl captures of official pages): Official Birmingham course page (fee in the page's embedded data behind the country selector); full-time, September start. Round 7 (2026-10-13, Common Crawl captures of official pages): The £34,740 is the September 2026 fee, not just a January figure. It appears on the September-intake page, with 2026 deadlines and the label 'September or January start'. Birmingham cut both its UK and international fees for 2026 entry (UK £13,040 to £12,150; international £36,000 to £34,740), then set £36,000 again for September 2027.
